label: EU(7)-PIM: acarbose
title: Acarbose in an older person
statement: Acarbose | In lists: does not appear as PIM | Main reason: No proven efficacy | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Diet; metformin (<2 x 850 mg/d); insulin; gliclazide may be safer than the other short-acting sulphonilureas. E

plain_summary: The EU(7)-PIM panel included acarbose, a diabetes tablet, because it found no proven benefit in older people. The words “does not appear as PIM” refer to the six earlier lists the authors compared.

medicine_groups.name: Acarbose
medicine_groups.note: Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (acarbose) is supplied, at any dose, to a patient aged 65 years or over. If age is missing and the other requirements are met, report only a possible finding and ask for the patient's age. One supply is enough. A patient aged under 65 years is not a finding.
cannot_be_seen: Blood glucose and HbA1c may be available in dated result rows. Supplies alone do not show these results, whether acarbose is helping, side effects such as wind and diarrhoea, how long it was used before this history starts, or whether doses are taken.
ask_the_gp: A review of whether acarbose is still helping the patient's diabetes control.
